Dr. Bobbie Ekman, a Grafton dentist and owner of Byrdie's martini bar, squeezes lemons and preps the bar before customers arrive. The Trust Project What is this? GRAFTON, N.D. — It's been a warm summer in Grafton, just like everywhere else. But downtown, Byrdie's martini bar is making people stop and look twice. ADVERTISEMENT One night a week, on Thursdays, people are putting on their cocktail dresses and fancy party clothes for martini night at Byrdie's, 500 Hill Ave. "It is like a dream fulfilled. When you are putting together all the plans and materials, you never are certain it will all go together," said Dr. Bobbie Ekman over the sound of a martini shaker. Bartenders and employees prepare drinks and serve customers during a night of cocktails at Byrdie's martini bar in downtown Grafton. Abby Makay / WDAY Ekman is a popular dentist in town, but she also owns a clothing-gift shop downtown. Next door was an old landmark. Polly's bar. Bobbi and her husband bought the building and began knocking down walls. "When we first walked in here, it had all been modernized in the 1950s, so most people today won't know there was a tin ceiling underneath," Bobbie said. And now — a bar from Egypt. Wallpaper from Poland. Trained bartenders and a crowd. Every Thursday night. "They went out of their way to energize downtown Grafton, which is a big deal when many small towns are dying. They are bringing energy to downtown," said customer Kylen Kostrzewski. The table and seating area inside Byrdie's martini bar in downtown Grafton is ready for guests on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026. Abby Makay / WDAY "You build what you want and we longed for a place to go to have a date night or a cocktail. We wanted something a little fancy," Bobbie said. ADVERTISEMENT There are a lot of legends in the old Grafton bar. A covered up wall, where, back in the day, they served liquor during Prohibition. "You can see the outline. Gentleman would go back there for cocktails, we assume," Bobbie said. Family and friends staff the special night every week. Making and delivering Manhattans, Gibsons and Lemon Drops. A chance to 'Put on the Ritz' in downtown Grafton. "My message is, don't be afraid to take a risk," Bobbie said of starting a new business. A candle sits in front of a drink menue at Byrdie's in downtown Grafton. Abby Makay / WDAY And the name "Byrdie's" has a little history — a great-aunt of the owner. Martini night at Byrdie's is 7:30 to 10:30 p.m. Thursdays. The business is also open for meetings and group events.
